focus: Cross-surface consistency, hardcoded-root contradictions and runtime configurability
noveltyJustification: Cross-checking producer, consumer, gate and documentation contracts exposed identity contradictions that a uniform direct-link model cannot satisfy.
keyQuestions: What would break when .opencode becomes a consumer link?
Which runtime configurability claims remain UNKNOWN after repository-only inspection?
answeredQuestions: OpenCode root resolution and MCP launch require a resolvable .opencode compatibility namespace.
Hermes scanner constraints and split agent dialects prevent a uniform direct-link topology.
Gates and documentation have different live/historical treatment.

ruledOut.approach: Use one direct .skilled link for every runtime directory
ruledOut.reason: OpenCode launcher, Hermes scanner behavior and split runtime dialects require different consumer shapes.

keyFindings.finding: The root helper, trigger index and OpenCode launcher all treat .opencode as a resolvable identity; a consumer link can work only if those contracts remain satisfied or are changed.
Hermes cannot safely consume the whole canonical tree and Codex/Pi/Hermes versus Cursor/Devin use different agent sources.
Pre-commit/pre-push scope is .opencode-based and markdown includes both live contracts and historical records.
